title: pvClipClosedSurface
body:
## pvClipClosedSurface

Clips a closed, manifold polygonal surface with a plane and caps the cut with new faces, so the result is again a closed (watertight) surface, e.g. to cut a CAD solid or an STL body and still compute its volume. Output is polydata; GenerateCellOrigins can add cell scalars that distinguish original faces from cap faces. Use clip or pvClip for volume meshes.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The input must be closed and manifold (no open edges, no edges shared by more than two faces); otherwise caps are wrong or missing. Check with featureEdges first.
- Face orientation defines the solid side: back faces must face the interior.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `ClipClosedSurface`. Identity: `filters/ClipClosedSurface`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the dataset on which the Clip filter will operate. Accepted data: polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BaseColor` | Specify the color for the faces from the input. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipColor` | Specify the color for the capping faces (generated on the clipping interface). | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClippingPlane` | This property specifies the parameters of the clipping plane used to clip the polygonal data. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Plane"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Plane"}` |
| `ClippingTolerance` | Specify the tolerance for creating new points. A small value might incur degenerate triangles. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `GenerateCellOrigins` | Generate (cell) data for coloring purposes such that the newly generated cells (including capping faces and clipping outlines) can be distinguished from the input cells. | `{"type":"enum","values":["None","Color","Label"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"None"` |
| `GenerateFaces` | Generate polygonal faces in the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `GenerateOutline` | Generate clipping outlines in the output wherever an input face is cut by the clipping plane. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `InsideOut` | If this flag is turned off, the clipper will return the portion of the data that lies within the clipping plane. Otherwise, the clipper will return the portion of the data that lies outside the clipping plane. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `ClippingPlane` → `Plane`

Syntax: `{"type":"Plane","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Plane`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClippingPlane.options.Normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClippingPlane.options.Offset` | Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ClippingPlane.options.Origin` | A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
